The attack – which also sparked fires at an oil refinery and depot – comes as Kyiv accused Russia of violating Washington's "energy ceasefire" dozens of times.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery
articles.summary: The Pope's first event since his lung cancer diagnosis and surgery saw him recite the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.

articles.title: ‘Austerity is inevitably painful’: How Michael Gove justifies his politics | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty
articles.summary:
For more than three decades,  Michael Gove  has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins  Aditya Chakrabortty  to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam  Watch the full episode with Michael Gove  here .

articles.title: Macron denounces 'unbridled' violence as France hit by new clashes
articles.summary: President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday slammed the "unbridled" violence that erupted in cost-of-living protests across France, as police battled protesters and looters in new clashes in Paris. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested and at least 1,000 police and gendarmes injured, the interior ministry said. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

articles.title: How day of protests unfolded as disorder breaks out across France
articles.summary: Demonstrations across the country turned violent, with cars and buildings set alight and shops ransacked.

articles.title: Briton threatened with deportation from Sweden over Brexit rules goes into hiding
articles.summary: Mark Smith, who has severe health issues, says he was told three times he needed to do nothing in order to remain after Brexit  A seriously ill British man living in Sweden has been forced into hiding amid fears he will be deported as a result of what he says is a government Brexit residency error.  Mark Smith, 60, who has had heart attacks, strokes, severe headaches and chronically high blood pressure that has been difficult to treat, was told on the phone he should leave Sweden by 17 October as he was an “alien” without permission to stay. articles.title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV was released from the hospital on Saturday after lung cancer surgery. Doctors removed part of the 71-year-old's right lung last week to extract a cancerous tumour.

articles.title: Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal
articles.summary: For 15 months, a high-security courtroom in Hamburg has been hearing the case of Christina Block, accused of ordering the abduction of her children.

articles.title: Zelensky fears Trump 'will continue' to lift Russia sanctions
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that he feared his US counterpart Donald Trump "will continue" lifitng sanctions on Russia. Zelensky's relationship with Trump deteriorated after the Washington eased sanctions on Moscow as part of a diesel-supply deal, despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine.

articles.title: 'Finish what we started': After student protests, France braces for return of the Yellow Vests
articles.summary: An online movement against rising fuel prices has gained momentum ahead of planned nationwide demonstrations on October 17 with former Yellow Vest figures set to join the protests in support of high-school students. Some are drawing parallels between the latest action and the 2018 cost-of-living protests that rattled President Emmanuel Macron's first term in office.

articles.title: Clashes grip Tirana as Albanian PM blames 'foreign hands' for mounting unrest
articles.summary: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Friday blamed the involvement of “foreign hands” for escalating protests, which he said are aimed at hindering Albania's bid to join the European Union. Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Albania's capital since Tuesday, demanding Rama’s resignation and denouncing university conditions and high tuition fees.

articles.title: Trump vs Zelensky, From the screen to the streets, Gen Z protests from Paris to Dehli
articles.summary: Our panel of international correspondents look back at the week's news, from protests in India to a blame game in Ukraine.

articles.title: 'US tilting toward Russia: Europeans are standing more and more solidly with Zelensky'
articles.summary: As transatlantic relations confront renewed geopolitical uncertainty, former Estonian president Toomas Hendrik Ilves delivers a pointed assessment of Washington's shifting approach to Russia's war on Ukraine and the profound implications for European security. At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental question: can Europe develop the political unity, strategic independence and military capabilities necessary to defend its interests in an increasingly unpredictable international order? Ilves' response: "If there's any time for Europe to begin to act as Europe and not as being strictly self-interested, then this is the time for it."

articles.summary: The BBC joins Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi as it regains crucial territory in the Donbas, but optimism has been dampened by souring relations with President Trump.

articles.summary: Zelensky thanked the "real leaders" ahead of a meeting with the EU in Brussels.

articles.title: The risks faced by women migrants in Europe
articles.summary: This October marks 10 years since French police dismantled the notorious Calais "Jungle" camp. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin returns to the region to explore what has changed for migrants over the past decade. She joins Annette Young and Dr Marissa Quie of Cambridge University to discuss migration routes and their growing role in European political debate.

articles.title: Albanian protests turn violent: What we know
articles.summary: Albania's capital Tirana has seen months of protests from an anti-government "Flamingo" movement, but what started on Tuesday this week was on a different scale.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass in hospital while recovering from lung cancer operation
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, photos released by the Vatican showed. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but that further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.

articles.title: 'America, with this president, is not our ally. Trump is a liar': French MEP Bernard Guetta
articles.summary: Our guest is veteran French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, who is a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group. He tells the programme that Donald Trump is "a liar, because he tried to tell the American people that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the price of diesel. This is a pure lie. He (Trump) is responsible because he started the war with Iran." Guetta goes on to say that "without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is weaker and weaker. That's terrible, to see the president of the United States giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine."

articles.title: Fuel prices in Dushanbe rise again: How much have they increased in three weeks?
articles.summary: Since late September, diesel fuel has seen the most notable price increase — by nearly 6%.

articles.title: EU and Canada seek closer ties: Will Canada become the EU's first associate member?
articles.summary: As the international context becomes more challenging for the European Union, the bloc is looking to boost its ties with like-minded allies. Canada is part of that architecture that the EU says it wants to build. The big news of EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's State of the Union speech in September was that Canada could become an associate member – an arrangement that does not exist for the EU's partners at the moment.

articles.title: Russia expands grounds for deporting foreigners with dangerous infectious diseases
articles.summary: A deportation order may now be issued not only following a mandatory medical examination, but also on the basis of a hospital's report of a detected infection.

articles.title: Tajikistan to develop database on nutritional value of food products
articles.summary: It will allow users to find out how many calories, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals various food products contain.

articles.title: Tajikistan and Iran discuss expanding transport and transit cooperation
articles.summary: Tajikistan and Iran discuss ways to expand bilateral cooperation in transport and transit; photo: IRNA.

articles.title: UK bookstores scramble as Sally Rooney's novels pulled over Palestine Action support
articles.summary: Critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney's announcement that her books could no longer be sold in the UK due to her support for proscribed group Palestine Action has left British booksellers rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out. The British government's ban on the group, which practiced non-violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government, makes support for Palestine Action punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

articles.title: Ukraine's backers will 'be looking at' Kyiv's €70 billion request, Macron says
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said the EU will “not abandon Ukraine and the Ukrainian people” and that Kyiv’s request for extra funds will be examined, while addressing the media at a summit in Brussels Friday. Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked EU leaders to provide Kyiv with an extra €70 billion next year to help with the country's ongoing fight against Russia. Read about the day’s events as they unfolded on our liveblog.

articles.title: Minibus crashes into train at French Channel Tunnel entrance, injuring 19
articles.summary: Nineteen people were injured Thursday when a minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a vehicle shuttle train at the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel near Calais, forcing a 90-minute suspension of shuttle services. Two people were hospitalised with serious but non-life-threatening injuries, French authorities said.

articles.title: France and Germany agree to ease EU car emissions rules in new deal
articles.summary: Paris and Berlin on Friday confirmed their deal aimed at protecting Europe's struggling automotive sector, having reached agreements on the flashpoint issues of EU car emissions and "made in Europe" components. A draft deal reviewed Thursday showed the two countries backing looser EU emissions rules for carmakers.

articles.title: Zelensky rallies European allies as US support for Ukraine wanes
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky sought European backing Thursday after vowing to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries despite US President Donald Trump’s demands to stop. Tensions between Kyiv and Washington have escalated in recent days over sanctions, energy infrastructure attacks and restrictions on satellite communications.

articles.title: Sally Rooney's books cannot be sold in UK amid Palestine Action ban, publisher says
articles.summary: Irish author Sally Rooney can no longer sell her books in the UK because of her support for the activist group Palestine Action, her publisher Faber said on Wednesday. Rooney has previously expressed her support for the group, which was banned as a "terrorist" organisation by the UK government in July 2025. It is not banned in Ireland, where Rooney lives. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Alan Greene, Professor of Constitutional Law and Human Rights at the Birmingham Law School.
